To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

open reduction and stable internal fixation of the tibio-talar and tibio-fibular joint should be done in a staged fashion, with the initial procedure consisting of external fixation and limited internal fixation of the distal fibula and the second procedure, 10 to 14 days later, consisting of definitive open reduction and internal plating of the distal tibio-tibial joint.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the management of high energy, open tibial plaffond fractures.
the development of a new technique of open reduction and internal plate fixation of the tibio-talar articular surface.
the treatment of the open fracture of the tibia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the treatment of tibial platon fractures is not clear.

open reduction and stable internal fixation of the tibiofibular joint and tibial plaffond with the use of the most appropriate internal fixation device is the optimal treatment for tibial pilion fractures.

high energy fractures of the tibio-talar plafond are best treated with early external fixation and limited internal fixation to restore length and then definitive open reduction and internal plating of the articular surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
open reduction and stable internal fixation is indicated for all tibial pilons.
the tibial pilond fracture can be managed successfully with open reduction and stable internal fixation.
the treatment of tibial plaffond fractures can be divided into two types, the low energy rotational type and the high energy compression type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
open reduction and rigid internal fixation can be done in high energy pilon injuries.
high energy pilion fractures should be temporised with an external fixater with or without fibula plating to restore the length.
open reduction and fixation of the tibio-talar joint is a viable treatment option for tibial platon fractures, and that it should not be abandoned as a viable option.
